result.summary: Pausanias describes the coast of Boeotia from Creusis to Thisbe and Tipha, then turns inland to Haliartus. At Haliartus, the tomb of Lysander prompts a balanced assessment of his victories, his justice and his harmful acts.

scenes.title: Coastal voyage: Creusis, Thisbe, Tipha
scenes.summary: Pausanias describes Creusis, the rough sea route, and the towns of Thisbe and Tipha with their temples of Hercules. Tipha claims the pilot Tiphys and the Argo's mooring place.

scenes.title: Haliartus and Lysander's tomb
scenes.summary: Inland at Haliartus, Pausanias notes its stance in the Persian invasion and the tomb of Lysander, killed attacking the city.
scenes.stakes: Haliartus faces burning by Xerxes' army; Lysander falls in battle.

scenes.title: Assessment of Lysander
scenes.summary: Pausanias weighs Lysander's naval victories and justice against his cruelty, his Decemvirates and the money-love he brought to Sparta. He concludes Lysander harmed Sparta more than he helped.
scenes.stakes: Sparta's moral and political standing is ruined by Lysander's actions.

notable_quotes.reason: Pausanias frames his balanced verdict on Lysander's character.

analysis.text: Pausanias pairs geography with local lore and uses a tomb to launch a moral judgment of a famous man.
His verdict reflects a Greek view of Spartan decline through greed and Lysander's imperial arrangements after the Peloponnesian War.

fun_facts.text: Lysander died at Haliartus in 395 BC, at the outset of the Corinthian War.

language_notes.text: "Haven" means harbour; Creusis served as the port of the Thespians, on the Corinthian Gulf.
"Circuitous" means roundabout; the coast's headlands force ships to take a winding course rather than a straight crossing.
The clause means the plain would naturally be a lake; only the embankment and yearly diversion of water keep it farmland.
Tiphys was helmsman of the Argo, the ship of Jason and the Argonauts, who sailed to Colchis for the Golden Fleece.
Pausanias refers to his earlier account of Orchomenus, where he treated the founder of Haliartus and Coronea.
"The Medes" means the Persians; Xerxes invaded Greece in 480 BC.
Alcibiades left his pilot Antiochus in charge, against orders, and Antiochus provoked a fight at Notium (406 BC), where Lysander defeated him.
Pancratiast: a competitor in the pancratium, a brutal athletic contest combining wrestling and boxing.
Pyrtaneum is Pausanias' spelling of the Prytaneum, the town hall at Athens, where honoured statues stood.
Decemvirates were ruling boards of ten men, set up by Lysander to control subject cities in Sparta's interest.
Harmosts were Spartan governors placed in subject cities.
Pausanias refers to the Persian rule, mentioned earlier in the chapter, that a man's good and bad deeds are weighed and the greater decides his worth.

context_notes.text: Hercules was widely worshipped in Boeotia as a hero-god, with festivals in many towns.
Greek cities often traced their names to local nymphs, minor female nature spirits tied to places.
Lysander, the Spartan admiral who defeated Athens in 404 BC, died at Haliartus in 395 BC, during the Corinthian War.
Aegospotami (405 BC) was the decisive battle ending the Peloponnesian War; Lysander surprised the Athenian fleet beached on the Thracian shore.
The Thirty Tyrants were the oligarchy imposed on Athens by Sparta after its defeat in 404 BC.
Marathon (490 BC) and Thermopylae (480 BC) were Persian War battles; the examples show that even enemies honoured the dead.

literary_notes.text: The townsfolk's claims, reported as "they say" and "they record", show Pausanias's cautious narrative voice, distancing himself from unverified local tradition.
The great conqueror of Athens dies before a small Boeotian town, aided by Athenian troops, a reversal of his earlier fortunes.
The balanced opening frames Lysander as a mixed figure, structuring the whole passage as a ledger of virtues and vices.
Athenian and Persian kindness to enemy dead sharpens the shame of Lysander's refusal of burial.
Sparta's oracle warned against avarice, yet its victorious general introduced the very vice that would ruin it.
